comment: Shared decision table for SpfnContractBinding.requireSupported / SPFNContractBinding.requireSupported. Both platforms read this file, so a rule that drifts on one of them fails there instead of being discovered against a real server. Hand-written on purpose: these are the cases a reviewer asked for, and deriving them from the same code they test would prove nothing.
rule: supported when the candidate parses as strict SemVer, carries the same pre-release as the lower bound, is at or above the lower bound, and is strictly below the upper bound

cases.why: the pinned version itself
a later patch on the pinned minor is additive
build metadata carries no precedence
below 1.0.0 the minor is the breaking axis; this is the case that made the rule necessary
a pre-release of a version outside the range is still outside it
a pre-release precedes its release, so it is below the lower bound
below the lower bound
another major
a client pinned at 0.1.5 needs what 0.1.0 does not carry
the lower bound is inclusive
at and above 1.0.0 the minor is additive
the upper bound is exclusive
a missing patch is not SemVer
a fourth component is not SemVer
a signed component is not a numeric identifier
a leading zero is not a numeric identifier
leading whitespace
trailing whitespace
an empty component
a version prefix is not part of SemVer
an empty pre-release identifier
empty build metadata
an empty identifier inside the pre-release
the empty string
not a version at all
full-width digits are not ASCII numeric identifiers
a patch far beyond Int must compare, not overflow
a major far beyond Int is still another major
a pinned pre-release accepts exactly itself
a different pre-release is a different contract
the release of a pinned pre-release is not the pinned contract
